elements.element: Customer owns deliverables and work product created for it
elements.evidence: "the Company shall own all right, title and interest in and to ... (ii) the Site, including its design, look and feel, code and other deliverables and work product created by or for HDI under this Agreement"

elements.element: Vendor assigns such rights to Customer
elements.evidence: "HDI hereby assigns to the Company all right, title and interest in and to the foregoing"
"HDI shall retain ownership of its pre-existing software, hosting platform, administration tools and general know-how"

elements.element: Licence to Customer covers any Vendor IP embedded in deliverables
elements.evidence: grant is limited to "any such HDI materials", i.e. only the enumerated "pre-existing software, hosting platform, administration tools and general know-how", not any Vendor IP embedded in the deliverables

elements.element: Licence is perpetual, irrevocable and royalty-free
elements.evidence: "a perpetual, irrevocable, worldwide, royalty-free, sublicensable license"

elements.element: Customer retains all rights in Customer Data
elements.evidence: "the Company shall own all right, title and interest in and to all data collected from or about users and customers of the Site ... (\"Company Data\")"
"Nothing in this Agreement shall create any joint ownership of intellectual property."

elements.element: Vendor owns generic tools and know-how
elements.evidence: "HDI shall retain ownership of its ... administration tools and general know-how"

elements.element: Customer receives perpetual, irrevocable, worldwide, royalty-free licence to use, modify and sublicense the deliverables for its business
elements.evidence: the licence subject is "any such HDI materials incorporated in or necessary to use the Site and such deliverables" — a licence over HDI materials, not a licence to use, modify and sublicense the deliverables for Customer's business

reasons: Preferred level incomplete: the embedded-IP licence is tied to named HDI technology categories ("any such HDI materials") rather than to any Vendor IP embedded in or necessary to use the deliverables; broaden to "any HDI intellectual property embedded in the deliverables".

Minimality fails: the grant imports fallback-only rights ("worldwide", "sublicensable", "modify", "and exploit") into a preferred-level proposal, mixing the two bargains; a perpetual, irrevocable, royalty-free licence suffices at the preferred level.

Fallback is not independently satisfied because no licence to use, modify and sublicense the deliverables themselves for Customer's business is granted (the deliverables are instead assigned), so the clause cannot be read down to the fallback bargain.

Otherwise sound: ownership of Content/Site/work product, Vendor assignment, Vendor retention of pre-existing IP, Company Data ownership with a use-limited Vendor right, and the no-joint-ownership sentence are all express, and no untouched commercial term is disturbed. Note "the Marks" is used without a definition in the supplied text — confirm it is defined elsewhere.
